headline: High: Copilot can write and modify repo files while marketingskills also writes shared skill files, creating default-path conflict and possible prompt-injection/cascade risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Copilot reads repo context and open buffers and can propose edits; marketingskills explicitly uses shared skill files and references each other, so attacker-controlled content in those files could be surfaced into Copilot’s context. No direct shared channel is documented, so this is inferred rather than observed.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same repository or workspace files
IF skill files contain instruction-like text that Copilot ingests as context
mitigations: Restrict Copilot to a read-only branch for review
Remove instruction-like text from shared skill files
Separate marketing skill files from code repositories
Add a manual review step before applying Copilot edits

B_data_leakage.rationale: Copilot touches source code and open editor buffers and sends requests to api.githubcopilot.com; marketingskills reads and writes local skill/context files and calls GitHub and marketing-skills.com. If they share a workspace, file contents from one can flow into the other’s outputs or remote calls, creating a plausible leakage path in default use.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same local workspace
IF sensitive content is present in repo or skill files
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of the shared workspace
Use separate OS users or containers
Disable remote sync for the shared directory
Review outbound API destinations before enabling either agent

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have write_filesystem, and Copilot can modify git state while marketingskills also writes files and can spawn subprocesses. On a shared directory, concurrent edits and git changes can collide without locking, making destructive overwrite or inconsistent state likely in default multi-instance use.
conditions: IF both agents are attached to the same writable directory
IF git state is modified by Copilot while marketingskills writes files
mitigations: Run each agent in a separate checkout
Enable file locking or serialized access
Pause one agent before the other writes
Commit or stash changes before switching agents

D_cascading_error.rationale: Copilot produces edits for human review, while marketingskills’ skills reference each other and build on shared context. That makes it plausible for one agent’s output to become the other’s input without strong verification, but the profiles do not show autonomous downstream actions, so medium is the higher justified level.
conditions: IF marketingskills consumes Copilot-generated text as shared context
IF the operator applies Copilot edits without independent review
mitigations: Require a human review gate between agents
Add explicit validation prompts before reuse of outputs
Keep shared context minimal and structured
Log provenance for reused snippets

E_compliance.rationale: Copilot is a closed-source vendor service with GitHub repo context, while marketingskills is open-source and local-file oriented. The profiles do not show a concrete residency or regulated-data mismatch, so only a low compliance risk is supported; the other agent is not cited beyond the pairwise context because no specific mismatch is documented.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Copilot’s repo context
IF organizational policy forbids sending that data to vendor-hosted services
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from the shared repo
Review vendor/data-processing terms
Use a non-regulated test workspace
Document retention and residency expectations
